Supporting captured files in this directory: - `list-options.txt` — combined stdout+stderr of `--list-options` (line 1 `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` is stderr) - `list-options.stdout.txt` — stdout only (326 lines, the full option list) - `list-options.stderr.txt` — stderr only (just `CROWBOOK 0.17.0`) - `create-output.txt` — byte-exact stdout of `--create a.md b.md` - `no-book-arg.stderr` — byte-exact stderr when no BOOK argument is given --- ## 1. General output conventions (non-TTY) - Exit code is **almost always 0**, even for hard errors (missing config file, missing chapter file, invalid options, render failures). Nonzero exits observed: - **2** for clap CLI-usage errors (bad flag values, missing required args). - **101** for a Rust panic (see §9, `--to html.dir -o`). - On startup the banner `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` is printed to **stderr** (not stdout). - Successful renders print nothing except the banner (default, non-verbose). - Errors are printed to stderr as `ERROR `; warnings as `WARNING `. - If errors/warnings occurred but the program still finished its run, they are preceded by the line (verbatim): ``` WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred: ``` Fatal single errors (abort before any rendering) are printed directly as `ERROR ...` without that preamble. - Option-conversion errors (unknown keys, wrong types) do NOT abort rendering; the offending option keeps its previous/default value and rendering proceeds (exit 0). - Chapter-list errors and YAML syntax errors abort the whole run (no output, exit 0). ### Flag variants change the stderr format Given `unknown.book` with keys `foo: bar` and `author.name: John`: - Default (non-TTY): ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred: ERROR unknown.book:2: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'foo' ERROR unknown.book:3: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'author.name' ``` - With `-q` / `--quiet`: banner suppressed; messages become bracket-log style (INFO lines still hidden): ``` [ERROR] unknown.book:2: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'foo' [ERROR] unknown.book:3: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'author.name' ``` (So `-q` does NOT silence errors; it only changes the format and hides the banner/INFO.) - With `-n` / `--no-fancy`: banner kept, bracket-log style, and INFO lines appear: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 [ERROR] unknown.book:2: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'foo' [ERROR] unknown.book:3: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'author.name' [INFO] Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): nf.html ``` (Note the upstream typo "Succesfully".) - With `-v` / `--verbose`: env_logger-style lines with timestamps on stderr, e.g.: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 08:59:36 [DEBUG] (1) crowbook::book: Ignoring YAML block: 08:59:36 [DEBUG] (1) crowbook::book: Attempting to generate html... 08:59:36 [DEBUG] (1) epub_builder::toc: rendered elem: "
  • 1. Chapter One
    • " 08:59:36 [INFO] crowbook::book: Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): v.html ``` ### No BOOK argument `crowbook` (no args), or `--set title X` without a book: exit **0**, stdout empty, stderr byte-exact (saved in `no-book-arg.stderr`; note the trailing blank line, ends `\n\n`): ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR You must pass the name of a book configuration file. For more information try --help. ``` --- ## 2. `--list-options` / `-l` - Exit 0. Banner `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` on stderr; the option list on stdout (326 lines). - Full verbatim stdout saved in `list-options.stdout.txt` (and combined capture in `list-options.txt`). - `-q` and `-v` variants produce byte-identical stdout; `-q` also suppresses the banner. - `--list-options` combined with a BOOK argument still just lists options (exit 0). - The list is grouped under headings: `METADATA`, `ADDITIONAL METADATA`, `OUTPUT OPTIONS`, `RENDERING OPTIONS`, `SPECIAL OPTIONS`, `HTML OPTIONS`, `STANDALONE HTML OPTIONS`, `MULTIFILE HTML OPTIONS`, `EPUB OPTIONS`, `LATEX OPTIONS`, `RESOURCES OPTIONS`, `INPUT OPTIONS #[SERDE(FLATTEN)]` (note the literal `#[SERDE(FLATTEN)]` leak in the heading), `CROWBOOK OPTIONS`. - Each entry format (see capture): option name, then ` type: (default: )`, then a wrapped description. Types seen: `metadata`, `path`, `string`, `integer`, `boolean`, `list of strings`, `template path`. Defaults are printed as `not set`, bare values (`en`, `syntect`, `1`, `true`), or quoted (`""`, `"2cm"`, template strings). --- ## 3. .book config file format ### 3.1 Overall structure - The file is: an optional **options block** (parsed as YAML!), followed by the **chapter list**. Comments (`#`) and blank lines allowed anywhere in the options part. - **Once a chapter line appears, later `key: value` lines are an error.** Config: ``` title: Before + ch1.md author: AfterAuthor ``` → `ERROR after.book:3: Error parsing configuration file: found invalid chapter definition in the chapter list` (no output, exit 0). - A file with **only chapter lines** (no options) is rejected, as is an empty file or comment-only file: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR empty.book: Error parsing configuration file: "could not parse %{file} as a book file." Maybe you meant to run crowbook with the --single argument? ``` Note: literal `%{file}` placeholder leak, no line number, and the hint on a second line. (Some book-recognition heuristic requires at least one option-looking line.) - A file with options but **no chapters** is valid and renders an empty book. - CRLF line endings are handled fine. A UTF-8 **BOM is NOT stripped**: `\xEF\xBB\xBFtitle: BOM` yields `ERROR bom.book:1: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key '﻿title'` (the BOM is invisibly embedded in the key in the message); the key is ignored. ### 3.2 Options are YAML - Plain `key: value` lines are accumulated and parsed as one YAML mapping. Consequences: - Quoted strings work: `title: "Quoted: With Colon"` → title `Quoted: With Colon`. - YAML escapes work: `author: 'Single''Quote'` → `Single'Quote` (then typographic cleaning turns `'` into a curly `’` in output). - Folded scalars work: ``` description: >- folded scalar here ``` → `folded scalar here`. - **Indented continuation lines** also join with a single space (even without `>-`): ``` description: This is a long description that continues on the next line and a third line ``` → `This is a long description that continues on the next line and a third line`. - Trailing YAML comments are stripped: `author: x # comment` → author `x`. - Space before the colon is fine: `title : spaced` → `spaced`. - Flow lists work for list options: `output: [html, epub]`, `resources.files: [a.md, b.md]`. - Block lists work too: ``` resources.files: - foo.md - bar.md ``` - A bare string is NOT accepted for a list option: `resources.files: foo.md bar.md` → `ERROR list.book:2: Error converting BookOption: Expected a list as value for key resources.files, found String("foo.md bar.md")` - Invalid YAML in the options block aborts (no output, exit 0). Examples: - A line without a colon (`title` or `garbage line`) → `ERROR edge.book:2: Error parsing configuration file: YAML block was not valid YAML: while parsing a block mapping, did not find expected key at line 2 column 1` - `description: has: colon` → `ERROR edge.book:2: Error parsing configuration file: YAML block was not valid YAML: mapping values are not allowed in this context at line 2 column 17` (These are serde_yaml error texts appended after `YAML block was not valid YAML: `.) ### 3.3 Duplicate keys / overriding - Later assignment wins, silently. `title: First` then `title: Second` → `Second`. Same for `author`. No warning. ### 3.4 Unknown keys - Non-fatal. Each unknown key produces (file:line of the key): `ERROR :: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key ''` prefixed by the `WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred:` line; rendering still happens; exit 0. Dot-form unknown keys behave the same (`author.name: John` → `unrecognized key 'author.name'`). ### 3.5 Wrong value types — exact messages All non-fatal (option keeps default, rendering proceeds, exit 0). The YAML value's Rust debug form is shown: `String("...")`, `Integer(42)`, `Real("2.5")`, `Boolean(true)`, `Null`. - Integer option, string value (`rendering.num_depth: notanumber`): `ERROR wrongtype.book:2: Error converting BookOption: expected an integer as value for key 'rendering.num_depth', found String("notanumber")` (lowercase `expected`; same for `Real("2.5")`, `String("3")`, `String("3x")`.) Negative integers (`-2`) are accepted. - Boolean option (`rendering.initials`): ONLY lowercase `true`/`false` are valid. `True`, `FALSE`, `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `maybe` → `... expected a boolean as value for key 'rendering.initials', found String("True")` etc. `1`/`0` → `... found Integer(1)` / `Integer(0)`. - Metadata/string option (`title: 42`, `author: true`, `title:` (empty)): `ERROR types2.book:1: Error converting BookOption: Expected a string as value for key title, found Integer(42)` (capital `Expected` for string type — inconsistent with integer/boolean messages); `found Boolean(true)`; empty value → `found Null`. - List option given a string: `Expected a list as value for key output, found String("html, epub")`. ### 3.6 Chapter list syntax | Line form | Result | |---|---| | `+ file.md` | numbered chapter | | `- file.md` | unnumbered chapter (no `Chapter N` header in output) | | `+file.md` / `-file.md` | OK (space after sign optional) | | `N.+ file.md`, `N.+file.md` | chapter forced to number N (e.g. `1.+ sub/ch3.md`); **no whitespace allowed between `.` and the sign** | | `N.- file.md`, `N.-file.md` | same for unnumbered (`2.- ch2.md` OK) | | `1. + file.md` (space after dot) | `ERROR :: Error parsing configuration file: error.chapter_whitespace` — literal untranslated localization key, even with `-L en` or `-L fr` (fr translates only the prefix: `Erreur dans l'analyse du fichier de configuration : error.chapter_whitespace`). No output, exit 0. | | `1. + file.md` (double space) | same `error.chapter_whitespace` | | `++ file.md` | same `error.chapter_whitespace` | | `! Part`, `1.@ Part X` | same `error.chapter_whitespace` | | `= Part One`, `** ch2.md` | `ERROR :: Error parsing configuration file: found invalid chapter definition in the chapter list` | | `@ Part One` | **part definition** (see below) | | `@` (no title) | `ERROR :: Error parsing configuration file: found invalid part definition in the chapter list` | | ` + ch2.md` (indented chapter) | leading whitespace ignored → plain numbered chapter; no nesting | | `+ ch1.md # trailing comment` | `error.chapter_whitespace` (trailing content after filename not allowed) | | filename containing spaces (`+ my file.md`) | `error.chapter_whitespace` — spaces in chapter filenames unsupported | | `# comment` between chapters | OK (ignored) | Parts: `@ Part One` creates a part. In standalone HTML it renders as `

    Part I

    Part One

    ` (roman numeral by default), and the chapter counter resets after it (default `rendering.part.reset_counter: true`). Multiple spaces after `@` are trimmed (`@ Double Space` → title `Double Space`). Other chapter facts: - The same file may be listed twice; its content is included twice. - Missing chapter file: `ERROR :: Could not find file '' for book chapter` — aborts (no output), exit 0. With `-L fr`: `Impossible de trouver le fichier 'nope.md' pour book chapter` (partial translation). - Chapter paths are resolved **relative to the .book file's directory**, not the CWD. E.g. running from `/tmp` on `/tmp/obs/book1/cfgdir/outer.book` containing `+ ch1.md` fails with `Could not find file 'book1/cfgdir/ch1.md' for book chapter` (message shows config-dir-joined path); `+ ../ch1.md` works. ### 3.7 `import` option - `import: other.book` merges another config's options as **fallback defaults**: the importing file's own options always win, regardless of whether `import:` appears before or after them. Verified: main sets `author: MainAuthor`, imported sets `author: ImportedAuthor` + `title: ImportedTitle` → result author `MainAuthor`, title `ImportedTitle`. - Imports are **transitive** (A imports B imports C; nearest definition wins: main > impB > impA). - The imported file's **chapter list is ignored** — only options are merged (verified: imported chapters absent from output). - `output.*` from an imported file IS honored (imported `output.html: imported.html` caused that file to be rendered). - Import path resolves **relative to the importing config file's directory** (works even when crowbook is invoked from another CWD). Absolute paths work. - Missing import file is non-fatal (rendering proceeds, exit 0): ``` WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred: ERROR Could not find file 'nope_import.book' for book ``` (no file:line prefix, unlike chapter errors). --- ## 4. Path resolution summary | Path kind | Resolved relative to | |---|---| | chapter files in .book | the .book file's directory | | `import:` path | the importing .book file's directory | | `output.*` paths from config | the .book file's directory (verified: running from `/tmp`, `output.html: conf.html` wrote `/tmp/obs/book1/conf.html`) | | `-o/--output` CLI path | the **CWD** | | `output.base_path` | prepended to config `output.*` paths (dir must exist; not auto-created) | `output.base_path` failure message (dir missing): `ERROR Error rendering html: could not create file 'outputs/bp.html': 'No such file or directory (os error 2)` (note the unbalanced quote before `No such`). With `-o /nonexistent-dir/x.html`: `ERROR could not create file '/nonexistent-dir/x.html': 'No such file or directory (os error 2)`. Both exit 0. --- ## 5. `--set key value ...` - Takes **flat pairs** in one occurrence: `--set title "Set Title" author "Set Author"`. - Multiple `--set` flags are rejected by clap (exit 2): `error: the argument '--set ...' cannot be used multiple times` - Odd number of values → clap error (exit 2): `error: 2 values required by '--set ...'; only 1 was provided` - `--set` values override the config file (config `title: Config Title` + `--set title "Set Title"` → `Set Title`). - Values are YAML-typed: `--set rendering.num_depth 3 rendering.initials true` works. - `--set output "[html, epub]"` works and renders both formats to filenames derived from the .book basename (`basic.html`, `basic.epub`). - `--set output.html setout.html` alone (no `--to`) triggers HTML rendering to that path. - Precedence: **`-o` beats `--set output.`** (`--to html -o ocli.html --set output.html oset.html` → wrote `ocli.html` only). - Invalid `--set` key/value aborts rendering (no output), exit 0, message: `ERROR Error in setting key bogus.key: set.book:2: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'bogus.key'` `ERROR Error in setting key rendering.num_depth: set.book:2: Error converting BookOption: expected an integer as value for key 'rendering.num_depth', found String("abc")` (Note the odd embedded `set.book:2` — a line number into the config file.) --- ## 6. `--create ...` - Prints a template .book to **stdout**; writes no file. Byte-exact stdout for `crowbook --create a.md b.md` saved in `create-output.txt` (reproduced below). Note the inconsistent quoting: most template lines are wrapped in double quotes, but `## List of chapters`, the `+ ...` lines and blank separators are not. ``` "author: Your name" "title: Your title" "lang: en" "## Output formats" "# Uncomment and fill to generate files" "# output.html: some_file.html" "# output.epub: some_file.epub" "# output.pdf: some_file.pdf" "# Or uncomment the following to generate PDF, HTML and EPUB files based on this file's name" "# output: [pdf, epub, html]" "# Uncomment and fill to set cover image (for EPUB)" "# cover: some_cover.png" ## List of chapters + a.md + b.md ``` - Exit 0. Nonexistent input files are silently accepted (`--create a.md missing.md` just emits `+ missing.md`). - A positional BOOK argument is simply appended to the file list (`--create a.md b.md newbook.book` emits `+ newbook.book`). - `--create ... -o out.html` is rejected by clap unless `--to` is also given (exit 2): `error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n --to ` with usage `executable --to --create ... --output [BOOK]`. - `--create a.md b.md --to html -o out.html` runs fine (exit 0) but **ignores** `--to`/`-o`: still prints the template to stdout, creates no `out.html`. - `-q --create ...` suppresses the banner; template still printed. --- ## 7. `--to` / `--output` interactions - `--to` possible values (clap): `epub, pdf, html, tex, odt, html.dir`. Invalid value → exit 2, e.g.: ``` error: invalid value 'docx' for '--to ' [possible values: epub, pdf, html, tex, odt, html.dir] ``` `--to html,epub` → same error plus ` tip: a similar value exists: 'html'`. - `-o/--output` **requires `--to`** (clap, exit 2): `error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n --to ` usage: `executable --to --output `. There is no format-by-extension inference. - Config with `output.html: conf.html` + `output.epub: conf.epub` renders both. - `--to html` (no `-o`) restricts rendering to that format but **uses the config's `output.` path** (wrote `conf.html`, not `conf.epub`). - `--to html -o cli.html` overrides config outputs entirely (only `cli.html` written). - `--to epub` needs a zip: with no `zip` binary on PATH: `WARNING Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library` (still succeeds). - `--to pdf` without xelatex: `ERROR Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command 'xelatex'` (exit 0). - `--to odt`: accepted by clap but the renderer rejects it: `ERROR unknown format odt` (no output, exit 0). (Yet `output.odt:` appears in `--list-options`-era configs such as assets/test.book.) - **`--to html.dir -o dirout` PANICS** (exit 101). Verbatim stderr (PID varies): ``` thread 'main' (12797) panicked at src/lib/html_dir.rs:464:64: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Error { source: Source { file: Some("basic.book"), line: Some(7) }, inner: InvalidOption("option 'output.html.dir' is not present") } note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace ``` (i.e. `-o` fails to set `output.html.dir`; leaks the upstream source path `src/lib/html_dir.rs:464:64`.) With `output.html.dir: hdir_out` in the config, `--to html.dir` works (creates `chapter_000.html`, `print.css`, `stylesheet.css`, …), though this build also emits a template error about `{{favicon}}`: `ERROR Error compiling template: render error` with a `:8:7` / `{{favicon}}` / `reason: not found in this scope` snippet (exit still 0). --- ## 8. Misc flags touching parsing - `-L/--lang ` sets the runtime UI language; invalid values (`-L xx`) are silently accepted. `-L fr` translates some messages but not all (see §3.6; the `error.chapter_whitespace` key is untranslated in every language tried). - `-a/--autograph`: prints `Enter autograph:` on **stdout** (no newline observed in the captured prompt beyond the colon), reads one line from stdin; with stdin at EOF it just proceeds (exit 0). - `-f/--force-emoji`, `-S/--stats`, `-s/--single`, `--print-template` not explored here (other scopes). - Nonexistent book file: `ERROR Could not find file 'nosuch.book' for book` (exit 0). ## 9. Exit-code summary | Situation | Exit | |---|---| | success | 0 | | unknown key / wrong type in config or `--set` | 0 (renders, unless `--set` error which aborts render) | | missing chapter file, YAML syntax error, bad chapter line, options after chapters | 0 (no output) | | missing .book file, missing import, render failure (no xelatex, bad dir), unknown format odt | 0 | | no BOOK argument | 0 | | clap usage errors (bad `--to` value, `-o` without `--to`, duplicate `--set`, odd `--set` pairs) | 2 | | `--to html.dir -o` | 101 (panic) | REPORT_EOF echo "written"; wc -l /workspace/observations/options.md

payload.resultSummary:
Report complete. Summary of what was delivered to `/workspace/observations/`:

**Files written**
- `options.md` (404 lines) — the full report
- `list-options.txt` — combined verbatim capture of `--list-options` (line 1 is the stderr banner)
- `list-options.stdout.txt` / `list-options.stderr.txt` — stream-separated captures
- `create-output.txt` — byte-exact stdout of `--create a.md b.md` (verified identical to the block quoted in the report)
- `no-book-arg.stderr` — byte-exact stderr for the no-argument case (note trailing blank line)

**Key findings for implementers**
- **Streams/exit codes**: banner `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` goes to stderr; nearly every runtime error (missing config/chapter/import, bad option types, render failures) still exits **0**; exit 2 only for clap usage errors; exit **101** for a real panic.
- **Config format**: one YAML options block followed by the chapter list; options after the first chapter line are an error; full YAML works (quoting, folded scalars, flow/block lists, comments, continuation lines); later duplicate keys win silently; BOM is not stripped; CRLF is fine; options-less or empty files are rejected with a `%{file}` placeholder leak plus a `--single` hint.
- **Exact error messages** captured for unknown keys, all wrong-type combinations (`String/Integer/Real/Boolean/Null` debug forms, inconsistent `expected`/`Expected` capitalization), and YAML syntax failures.
- **Chapter syntax**: `+`/`-` (space optional), `N.+`/`N.-` (no space after the dot, else untranslated `error.chapter_whitespace`), `@ Part` parts, no nesting, no spaces in filenames, missing-file message with `file:line` prefix.
- **`import`**: transitive fallback-defaults merge (main always wins regardless of position), imported chapter list ignored, imported `output.*` honored, path relative to importing file; missing import is non-fatal.
- **Path resolution**: chapters/import/config `output.*` relative to the .book dir; `-o` relative to CWD.
- **`--set`**: flat pairs in one flag, YAML-typed values, overrides config, loses to `-o`; invalid pairs abort rendering (exit 0).
- **`--create`**: prints a quoted-line template to stdout only; `--to`/`-o` ignored (but clap requires `--to` if `-o` given); paths echoed verbatim.
- **Notable bugs**: `--to html.dir -o` panics leaking `src/lib/html_dir.rs:464:64`; `--to odt` accepted by clap but `ERROR unknown format odt`; `-q` doesn't silence errors, it switches to `[ERROR]` log format; `-n` adds `[INFO]` lines; `-v` gives timestamped DEBUG logs; partial French translations.

args.command:
cat > /workspace/observations/misc.md <<'REPORT_EOF' # Crowbook 0.17.0 — Misc features: stats, single-file mode, autograph, proofread, localization Binary: `/workspace/executable` ("crowbook 0.17.0 by Élisabeth Henry "). All tests run by observation only. Sample outputs referenced below are saved under `/workspace/observations/misc/`. ## 0. General CLI behavior relevant to all sections - When stdout is not a TTY, the first line on **stderr** is `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` (suppressed by `-q`). - **Exit codes**: virtually all runtime errors (missing book, missing chapter, render failure, unknown config key) still exit **0**. Only clap-level usage errors exit **2**, e.g. an invalid `--to` value or conflicting flags (`-v` with `-q`): ``` error: the argument '--verbose' cannot be used with '--quiet' ``` - `-v`/`--verbose` switches stderr to env_logger-style logs with timestamps, e.g.: ``` 09:16:19 [DEBUG] (1) crowbook::book: Ignoring YAML block: 09:16:19 [INFO] crowbook::book: Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): out.html ``` (note the typo "Succesfully"; also `Succesfully generated EPUB:`, `Succesfully generated LaTeX:`). Without `-v` a successful render prints **nothing** but the banner. - Chapter paths in a book config and output paths (`output.*`) are resolved relative to the **book file's directory** (and, in single-file mode, relative to the Markdown file's directory), not to the cwd. --- ## 1. `--stats` / `-S` ### 1.1 Exact output format Command (book and chapters saved in `misc/stats/`): ``` $ /workspace/executable --stats test.book ; echo EXIT=$? ``` stdout (byte-exact, see `misc/stats/stats_basic.stdout.txt`; stderr only has the banner): ``` Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word --------- chapter1.md 87 14 6.21 chapter2.md 116 19 6.11 --------- TOTAL: 203 33 6.15 ``` - The **entire table goes to stdout** (header included); stderr carries only `CROWBOOK 0.17.0`. - The output ends with the TOTAL line followed by a **blank line** (`...6.15\n\n`). - Layout: one row per chapter entry; a `TOTAL:` row at the end. Separator lines are **exactly 9 dashes** (`---------`), regardless of column width. - Column geometry (0-indexed, measured with several filename lengths): - name column width `W` = max **character count** (Unicode chars, not bytes) of the chapter filenames *as written in the book file* (e.g. `café.md` counts 7). `W` is NOT clamped to `len("Chapter")=7` — with shorter names the header overflows (see below). - data rows: `{name left-aligned, padded to W}{Chars right-aligned, 12 wide}{Words right-aligned, 11 wide}{Chars/Word right-aligned, 12 wide}` — no explicit separator spaces. So the Chars value's last digit is at column `W+11`, Words at `W+22`, ratio at `W+34`. - header row is fixed text: `Chapter` + `W` spaces + `Chars` + 6 spaces + `Words` + 2 spaces + `Chars/Word`. The column labels therefore right-align with the values. When `W < 7` ("Chapter" longer than the name column), the gap after `Chapter` shrinks accordingly (e.g. W=4: `Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word`, values still ending at 15/26/38). - `TOTAL:` row uses the same data-row format with the literal name `TOTAL:` (6 chars, padded to W or overflowing like the header). - Numbers: plain integers, no thousands separators (617279 observed); they simply overflow the field width when large. - `Chars/Word` = `chars / words` formatted with exactly 2 decimals. When a chapter has 0 words the ratio prints `NaN` (Rust's `f64::NAN` Display), e.g. an empty file: ``` empty.md 0 0 NaN ``` TOTAL uses the sums, not the average of ratios. ### 1.2 Counting rules (reverse-engineered) Model that reproduces every observed count: the renderer walks the parsed Markdown tokens of the chapter, concatenates their text into ONE string, then `chars = string.chars().count()` (Unicode scalar values) and `words = string.split_whitespace().count()` (Unicode whitespace). Consequences, all verified (inputs in `misc/stats/rules_inputs/`, outputs in `misc/stats/stats_rules{1,2,3}.txt`): - **No separator is inserted between blocks**: `aaa\n\nbbb` (two paragraphs) → 6 chars, **1 word** ("aaabbb"). A heading followed by a paragraph glues together: `# Title` + `aaa bbb` → "Titleaaa bbb" → 12 chars, 2 words ("Titleaaa", "bbb"). - **Headings count** (heading text included). Lists count ("- item one\n- item two" → "item oneitem two" = 16 chars, 3 words). Blockquotes count. - SoftBreak (single newline, incl. CRLF) counts as **1 char** and acts as a word separator: `hello\nworld` → 11 chars, 2 words; `a\r\nb` → 3 chars, 2 words (CR normalized away). - Trailing newline of the file does not count (`hello world\n` == `hello world` → 11). - Multiple inner spaces count as chars but not as words: `aaa bbb` → 10 chars, 2 words. - Tabs count as 1 char and split words. - Inline code counts (`` `code` `` → "code"); fenced code blocks count **including the trailing newline** (`para text` + fenced `code line here` → 24 chars = 9+15, 4 words). - **Inline HTML counts verbatim**: `text html more` → 21 chars (tags included), 3 words. - Images contribute nothing (alt text NOT counted): `text ![alt text](img.png) more` → "text more" → 10 chars, 2 words. - Footnote references (with a matching definition) contribute nothing; footnote *definitions* are not counted. An **unresolved** `[^1]` stays literal text: `aaa[^1]bbb` → 10 chars, 1 word. - Unicode: `café naïve` → 10 chars (é/ï = 1 char each); `😀 emoji test` → 12 chars (emoji = 1 char, i.e. scalar values not bytes); `日本語 テスト` → 7 chars, 2 words. - Word splitting is Unicode-whitespace based: NBSP (U+00A0) and figure space (U+2007) DO split words (`foo\u00A0bar baz\u2007qux` → 4 words). Punctuation tokens count as words: `l'élève dit « bonjour »` → 5 words (`«` and `»` are words); a free-standing `–` counts as a word; `one—two` (em dash, no spaces) is 1 word. - Counts are taken on the **raw source text**: `lang` and `input.clean` make no difference (French cleaning does not insert NBSPs before counting). - Book-config chapters listed with `+`, `-` (unnumbered) and `!` are ALL counted; the same file listed twice is counted twice. A part (`@ part.md`) produces a row with an **empty name** containing the part's display title text only (observed: 8 chars / 1 word = "part1.md", the filename fallback title; the part file's own Markdown body was not counted and did not render). ### 1.3 Interactions - `--stats` short-circuits rendering: `--stats --to epub -o x.epub test.book` prints the table and creates **no** output file (exit 0). - Works with `-s` single-file mode (`--stats -s chapter1.md` → one row, shown name = the md file). - `-q` suppresses the banner but the table still prints; exit 0. - `-v` adds this stderr line before the table (note typo "crowboook"): `[WARN] This version of crowboook has been compiled without support for advanced statistics` - `-a` still prompts (`Enter autograph:`) **before** printing stats. - Unknown keys in the book config print `[ERROR] file:line: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'foo'` on stderr but stats still run; exit 0. - Missing chapter: `ERROR missing.book:4: Could not find file 'nonexistent.md' for book chapter`, exit 0, no table.
